execution_envelope.distinction: The 600-second bounded execution turn is not the 900-second P0 acceptance window.

active_retest.purpose: Test guarded timing compensation against the measured scheduler-delivery segment while preserving single substantive authority and completion-relative fallback.
active_retest.promotion_rule: Do not promote predictive timing from one sample; rollback on unsafe overlap or failed useful-work handoff.

latest_diagnosis.evidence: The former +780s provisional made a normal ~10m turn appear to wait until ~13m. Manual near-due mutation proved the scheduler accepts earlier DTSTART, but prior controlled reservation A/B evidence found repeated +2m SHORT_ROLLING caused an overlapping duplicate invocation while +11m LONG_PROVISIONAL completed >600s with no observed overlap and low mutation churn. The 01:30:15 scheduled invocation also produced last_run_time without a matching new BOOT_STARTED by 01:33+, so invocation metadata alone is not bootstrap proof.
latest_diagnosis.implication: Use workload-relative adaptive +11m provisional for normal ~10m turns, no routine mid-turn mutation, exact END+60 at close, and distinguish scheduler invocation from durable BOOT_STARTED.

next_corrective_experiment.hypothesis: Earlier guarded same-canonical due placement can absorb observed delivery latency under predecessor useful work without creating dual substantive authority.
next_corrective_experiment.success_signal: Observed successor first-useful handoff materially reduces cross-turn loss with no duplicate substantive side effect or schedule rollback.
